∡ denotes directed angles modulo 180°. Let F be the foot of the perpendicular from B to AR. Angles written ∠ are undirected and read as drawn.

Claim 1. F, N, B, A are concyclic.

Proof. ∡BFA = 90° = ∡BNA (BF ⟂ AR; BC is a diameter), so F, N, B, A are concyclic.

Claim 2. FN = BF.

Proof. ∡FAN = ∡BAF (AR bisects ∠BAC). By equal arcs and chords (Claim 1), FN = BF.

Claim 3. R, N, F, O are concyclic.

Proof.

∡RFN = ∡BFN + 90°    [BF ⟂ AR]
     = 2∡FBN + 90°    [FB = FN (Claim 2)]
     = 2∡FAN + 90°    [inscribed angles in (ABNF) (Claim 1)]
     = ∡BAC + 90°    [AR bisects ∠BAC]
     = ∡MCN    [BC is a diameter]

As drawn, ∠MCN = ½·∠MON = ∠RON (central angle ∠MON = 2∠MCN; OR bisects ∠MON), so R, N, F, O are concyclic.

∡BPC = ∡BMR + ∡RPC    [P, R, M, B concyclic]
     = ∡BAC + ∡NRM    [P, R, N, C concyclic]
     = 2∡BNF + ∡NRM    [Claim 1, AR bisects ∠BAC]
     = ∡ORM + ∡ORN    [Claim 3, OF is the perpendicular bisector of BN (Claim 2)]
     = 0°    [△OMR ≅ △ONR (ASA), △ROM ≅ △RON (SAS), OM = ON]

so P, B, C are collinear. ∎
